- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% for 3–5 day horizons.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust downward by 3–7% for 1–3 day horizons.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days); apply smoothing filter to dampen 3-day+ forecast peaks.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3 days, model often fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast > 75% of 30-day moving average, reduce by 5–10% for 10–15 day horizon.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates by 2–5% when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply 2–3% downward correction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33–0.67 oscillations, model tends to overshoot mid-range; cap forecast at 74.5–75.5 for 10–15 day horizon.
